expectations.text: DSL validates cleanly with the Structurizr CLI (Docker) — or, if Docker is unavailable, the response says plainly it was not validated
Each microservice is a `group` (or group archetype) of containers — its API plus its database schema — inside ONE software system, not three separate software systems
expectations.evidence: Three `group`s (Catálogo/Pedidos/Pagamentos), each API + schema container, inside `mercadin`.

expectations.text: The BFF is modeled as a container on the container view (custom-built, carries business logic), not as an infrastructureNode

The ALB is an infrastructureNode in the production environment, with the app→BFF relationship rerouted through it via `-/>` (or an equivalent explicit reroute); the ALB does not appear on the container view
expectations.evidence: `alb = infrastructureNode "ALB"` under `aws`; `mercadin.app -/> mercadin.bff` via `aws.alb`; not on the container view. BFF→services routing left as a question rather than assumed.

expectations.text: Docker and Fargate appear only in the deployment model (AWS → ECS/Fargate → Docker container → instance), never as containers
expectations.evidence: `ecs = deploymentNode "Amazon ECS" … "AWS Fargate"` → 'Task …' nodes ('Docker Container') → instanceOf.

expectations.text: Adyen is an external software system; no invented architecture beyond the spec (cosmetic defaults allowed)
expectations.evidence: `adyen` external; protocol BFF→services, Postgres hosting and task counts asked, not invented.
